235: Effect of mesh convergence: the QHA F of fcc Al changes from [4,4,4] (64 q-points for the primitive cell) to 60 Å by −6.0 meV/atom at 700 K and −8.8 meV/atom at 900 K (bcc Li −1.7/−3.4, B32 −0.3). This raises the Al melting point from 850 to 890 K, consistent with example 4, which uses only calphy solid–liquid TI (902–927 K). The run-to-run spread of the liquid is 0.1–0.2 meV/atom (at most 0.55), and the Monte Carlo σ has a lower bound of 1.4 meV/atom. Error band (30 samples): fcc + liquid at 770 K is fcc 0.11 ± 0.03 and liquid 0.29 ± 0.02; at 850 K 0.04 ± 0.02 and 0.13 ± 0.05. The stability ranges of Al₂Li₃ and Al₄Li₉ at 690 K appear in 16 / 8 of 30 samples, so the decomposition temperatures carry a width of about ±20 K. Reducing the configuration noise does not change the eutectic temperature; the main reason the temperatures are about 100 K below experiment lies in the potential and the classical level. The composition features (congruent melting of B32, the stability-temperature order Al₂Li₃ > Al₄Li₉) agree with experiment, but the eutectic composition is shifted 0.07 towards Li from the experimental 0.24 (Okamoto 2012 Fig. 1, Hallstedt & Kim 2007 assessment). The source of the experiment column is 資料/10.1007/s11669-012-0119-8/Fig1_readings.md.

238: There is no public MLIP dedicated to Ni–Al, so the NIST Purja Pun & Mishin 2009 EAM is used. Key points per stage: in 01, NiAl₃ and Ni₂Al₃ lie 60–120 meV/atom above the convex hull (a known limitation of this EAM). 02A samples B2 with 54-site anti-site and vacancy cells and L1₂ with 108-site anti-site cells (the number was extended in stage 3). In 03A, because the stage-1 QHA gave an anomalous Ni melting point below 1500 K, the solid phases near the melting point were switched to calphy TI (QHA − TI = +43 (Ni), +36 (L1₂), +8–16 (B2) meV/atom). 04A moved from a triple-defect-type constitutional defect model to a thermal-defect (Wagner–Schottky) model in stage 4. Interpolation A fits the B2/L1₂ defect energies linearly per branch; stage 4 uses the model curve. On mygardenx1 (64 cores) the liquids (16 ranks × 3 runs) and the solids ran concurrently, about 1 hour for all 4 stages.

282: Lesson: the quasi-harmonic approximation cannot be used near the melting point. In stage 1 (QHA solids) the Ni melting point was below 1500 K and the B2 congruent melting 1739 K. About 18 meV comes from phonopy's fixed mesh (64 q-points for cells with a small primitive cell), the rest from anharmonicity. Above 0.8 T_m, use calphy TI for the solids too.
283: Why B2 has no width on the Al side (stage-5 supplement, vacancy_analysis.py): the point-defect formation energies of B2 NiAl in this EAM (pure-element reference, 128 sites) are Va_Ni 1.76, Va_Al 2.03, Ni_Al 0.51, Al_Ni 1.58 eV, triple defect (2 Va_Ni + Ni_Al) 2.82, anti-site pair 2.09, Schottky pair 2.58 eV, about 1.5 eV higher than the DFT triple defect of 1.0–1.3 eV (Fu–Painter 1997, Korzhavyi 2000). Shifting the Ni-vacancy free energy in the thermal-defect model by −0.2 / −0.4 / −0.6 eV moves the Al-side boundary at 1400 K to 0.495 / 0.468 / 0.400 (experiment about 0.45 at 1600 K). The missing width is a property of the potential's vacancy energies (0.4–0.5 eV per vacancy higher than DFT), not a problem of the workflow. The remedy is on the potential side (an MLIP whose training includes B2 vacancies and triple defects).
